conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Flip-Dot Display
style.description: A giant mechanical flip-disc sign: thousands of round discs, fluorescent yellow on one side and matt black on the other, physically flip on diagonal pivots in visible waves to form pictures and words, with a clatter made from the same flip plan.
motion: Nothing moves except discs flipping: every picture change is a set of single-disc flips from the flip plan.
A flip is a fast half turn on the diagonal axle that hits its stop at ~0.18 s and rebounds a few degrees; a settled disc is exactly still.
Changes travel as waves: a scan line, a ring from a point, row by row, or a seeded sprinkle; the front is ragged by a small per-disc delay.
Sound is the plan: one tick per lone flip, denser grains as more discs land in the same 1/30 s.
Camera: moves only while discs are flipping; holds are pixel-still. Close-ups from ~30 degrees off-axis show the half turn.

notes.mechanism: flipplan.js: a seeded noise bitmap, then denoisePasses(picture) at noise levels 1 / 0.9 / 0.78 / 0.6 / 0.08 / 0.03 / 0 (level 1 = pure noise, 0 = picture); createPlan turns each change of bitmap into single-disc flip events ordered by a scan / radial / random wave; each disc's angle is a closed form of its last flip.
notes.honesty: A simplified picture of diffusion: real models predict and remove noise in a learned latent space; here each pass re-rolls the still-noisy discs and fixes the rest.
